title: Four central banks broaden cooperation on settling regional transactions in local currencies
bank: Bank Indonesia, Bank Negara Malaysia, Bank of Thailand and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
summary: Bank Indonesia, Bank Negara Malaysia, the Bank of Thailand and Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas signed a common agreement on 13 November to facilitate settlement in local currencies. The change was institutional. The new memorandum superseded bilateral agreements signed among Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand in August 2023 and brought the Philippines into the four-authority arrangement. Individual transactions still take place between counterparties in two jurisdictions. Trade, investment and other eligible bilateral transactions are within scope (joint release, paragraphs 1–2).

The stated commercial case concerns conversion costs and flexibility in managing foreign-exchange exposure. A business choosing how to pay a supplier or settle an investment could benefit if a local-currency route avoids a series of conversions. Whether it saves money depends on the quotes and associated costs actually available for its amount and settlement date. Whether it reduces risk also depends on the currency of the underlying cash flows. Those conditions are implications for evaluating the initiative. The announcement gives no transaction-level prices or evidence that businesses have already achieved a saving (paragraph 3).

The governors committed to continue work on implementation. The authorities expected usage to expand gradually, supporting economic activity and regional financial cooperation over time. For an investor, the relevant horizons are therefore the agreement date, when cooperation was formalised, and the later dates when firms can transact and volumes can be observed. The publication specifies no numerical adoption target, effective date for a new product, committed amount of liquidity, or mechanism for stabilising any particular exchange rate. It offers no basis for translating signatures into a near-term directional forecast for local currencies (paragraph 4).

questions.question: Which transactions and currency pairs can businesses actually settle under the framework?
questions.detail: Trade and investment fall within the scope of the agreement, but firms still need to know which counterparties, payments and accounts qualify. The implementation details would determine whether an exporter can change its invoicing or settlement practice. Consult operating guidance and participating-bank notices from the four authorities, checking eligibility and launch dates separately for each bilateral corridor.

questions.question: Will the direct route lower all-in costs at the sizes firms need?
questions.detail: The authorities expect fewer conversions to improve efficiency. The release gives no executable spreads, fees or settlement times. For a treasury desk choosing between routes, collect simultaneous quotes for the same cash amount, value date and time of day, including both legs and fees on the existing route. Participating dealers’ quotes and published charges would test the prospective benefit.

questions.question: Will settlement in local currency change the exposure companies retain?
questions.detail: More settlement options may help firms manage currency risk. The effect depends on which currencies their sales, debt and input costs are denominated in, and whether hedges are available at the required maturity. Central-bank usage surveys, banks’ forward quotes and corporate treasury disclosures could show whether businesses reduce a mismatch or move it to a supplier or another part of their balance sheet.
